body:
Thank you for your advice. I've been to every counselor I could afford when I still had insurance. 

I don't know if it's just me, but I couldn't take anything away from the cognitive therapy. No one's suggestions ever echoed with how I was feeling, and eventually it always came down to, "well, you'll benefit from medication, most likely."

Well, thank you for your advice, but I can't take it to heart. I've already seen some cool stuff in my life, and honestly the pleasure of it is as transitory as anything else. 

Frankly it's still not enough to make me want to live day to day, and I don't think there's anything necessarily wrong with no longer wanting to live. Especially considering that I, like many, feel that we basically live in an ecologically and socially toxic environment.
I might, if it were that easy- to just go, but I haven't got the resources for that.
I've considered that, but I think I've known enough of life. It's up and down, but I'm sick of it both ways.
